name: Tourist / e-Visa

requirements.blocker_text: Citizens of 7 neighboring states (Russia, Kazakhstan, Belarus, Azerbaijan, Georgia, Armenia, Ukraine) enter visa-free with no time limit. Citizens of 76 further countries (including Germany, France, the UK, Canada, Brazil, Mexico, Japan, South Korea, Australia) enter visa-free for tourism for up to 30 days. Kyrgyzstan gets 60 days; Tajikistan 30 days; Bahrain/Kuwait/Oman 10 days with a return ticket required.

Citizens of 56 further designated countries (including the US, China, India, Vietnam, and most Middle Eastern and African countries) can obtain an e-visa via e-visa.gov.uz. Tourist e-visas (T) run up to 1 month. Fees range roughly $40-160 for single-entry, $150-350 for multiple-entry, depending on duration.
requirements.fix_path: Apply for the e-visa online with a passport valid at least 3 months beyond the visa's expiry.

evidence_required.document: Passport valid 3+ months beyond visa expiry

outcome.duration_length: up to 30 days (tourist); no limit for the 7 unrestricted-neighbor nationalities

sources.title: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Uzbekistan (gov.uz) -- official visa-free country lists, e-visa eligible countries via e-visa.gov.uz, visa categories, and consular fee schedule

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Uzbekistan). STATUS: PUBLISHED -- direct government sourcing (gov.uz, tier 1). e-visa.gov.uz itself returned only page metadata on direct fetch (a JS-rendered single-page app, not fetchable as static content), so the gov.uz Ministry of Foreign Affairs page was used as the authoritative source instead and confirms the same e-visa system by name. Uzbekistan's visa regime is notably liberal for a Central Asian state -- 83 countries combined get visa-free access, a marked contrast to several more restrictive countries built elsewhere in this dataset. dual_citizenship_allowed left null here since visitor status doesn't engage citizenship questions.
